metadata.title: Claude, K12 Lesson Planning.
metadata.subtitle: The K12 Lesson Planning Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude plans a lesson, is it improvising in the moment or following a set process? It's the latter — Claude reads the k12-lesson-planning skill's SKILL.md before acting and follows its written steps, using the folder's reference material and scripts rather than reasoning every step fresh. Lands the carry-out that the same request gets the same kind of result every run, and anything the steps don't cover falls back to Claude's own judgment.

beats.narration_text: Someone wonders if Claude plans a lesson by improvising in the moment. It doesn't — it follows a written set of steps. So: when Claude plans a lesson for your class, does it follow written steps?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. triggerWords/replacementWords must be a SINGLE whitespace token each (the component matches trigger against one split token's punctuation-stripped core; a multi-word trigger never matches and the correction silently never fires — confirmed as a defect on the k12-lesson-differentiation sibling built earlier this batch) and the trigger should be the LAST content word before terminal punctuation so nothing trails the replacement ungrammatically. 'improvise' is a single token immediately before the terminal '?', so this reel does not repeat that defect. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('improvise' -> 'follow written steps') lands on screen.

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is called k12-lesson-planning. Its SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set, in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The instructions live in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and executes it — read the file, execute each step, return the result. Linear: no branching, unless a step says otherwise.

production_viz.label: READ, EXECUTE, RETURN
production_viz.caption: linear — no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: One thing is worth knowing about this particular skill: it isn't only prose. Alongside SKILL.md, the folder ships a references folder and a scripts folder — supporting material and runnable code the skill uses directly. Where a step can run as code, it does, so the same step produces the same result, not a freshly-reasoned answer typed out each time.

production_viz.label: NOT ONLY PROSE
production_viz.caption: code where it can — not reasoned fresh each time

beats.narration_text: Claude isn't improvising the lesson plan — it's following the k12-lesson-planning skill's written steps, the same way every time. Ask for something those steps don't cover, and you get Claude's own judgment, not the skill's playbook.
